description:
Authentic Japanese Matcha Gelato at Home – A Creamy, Rich, and Flavorful Recipe! 🍵🍦

In today’s video, I’ll show you how to make authentic Japanese Matcha Gelato right at home! 🍃 Using premium, ceremonial-grade matcha powder, we’ll create a creamy, vibrant green gelato that captures the essence of traditional Japanese flavors. This recipe is perfect for matcha lovers, offering an incredibly smooth texture and the distinct umami richness that only high-quality matcha can bring. 🍵

I’ll guide you step-by-step through this easy, no-fuss recipe, from tempering the milk and cream to achieving that perfectly smooth consistency. Along the way, I’ll share tips on choosing the right matcha, handling the ingredients to get that deep green color, and ensuring that perfect balance of flavor and sweetness.

If you’re passionate about gelato or simply want to bring a taste of Japan to your kitchen, this video is for you! Don’t forget to give a thumbs-up if you enjoyed it and subscribe for more food science and dessert adventures! 🍨💚

Timestamps:
0:00 Intro
2:25 Ingredients
3:40 Preparing the Gelato Base
6:22 Churning the Gelato
7:30 Final Results & Tasting

comments.text: I have a question about the overrun. I used the same machine as you do. How do you control the level of overrun in any machines: do you let it churn longer or less, try to reach a temperature lower than -12C or higher?
comments.author: @elaf6533

comments.text: Overrun is really very difficult to control in small machines, commercial machines have air injection to control which home machines don’t have. Some ingredients can help increase it slightly. In home machines there really is only the “right churn time” as if you under churn you’ll have no overrun, over churn you’ll create fat globules. The ideal temperature is -12C but that is often not achievable with certain recipes. Some will harden before that temperature is reached. It’s all recipe dependent unfortunately.
